title: Understanding the Cross-Entropy Loss
text: Cross-entropy loss is used to measure the performance of a classification model whose output is a probability value between $$0$$ and $$1$$. It increases as the predicted probability diverges from the actual label.

title: Logistic Function
text: The logistic function, also known as the sigmoid function, is defined as \( \sigma(x) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-x}} \). It outputs a value between $$0$$ and $$1$$, which can be interpreted as a probability.

title: Calculate the Linear Combination
text: For the given passenger, calculate the linear combination of the features and parameters: \( $$z$$ $$=$$ $$-1.2$$ + $$(-0.005$$ \times 20) + $$(2.5$$ \times 1) \).

title: Apply the Sigmoid Function
text: Use the logistic function to find the predicted probability: \( \sigma(z) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-z}} \).

title: Cross-Entropy Loss Formula
text: The cross-entropy loss for a true label \( $$y$$ \) and predicted probability \( \hat{y} \) is given by \( -[y \cdot \log(\hat{y}) + $$(1-y)$$ \cdot \log(1-\hat{y})] \).

title: Calculate the Cross-Entropy Loss
text: Since the passenger survived, \( $$y$$ $$=$$ $$1$$ \). Compute the loss: \( -\log(\sigma(1.2)) \).
